script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. GYM - DAY

In the center of a bright, modern gym, CHARLES, mid-40s, sweats in a T-shirt and shorts. He's on the elliptical, his eyes fixed on a TV screening an old baseball game.

ELSEWHERE, COACH LUCAS, 50s, watches Charles, a twinkle of recognition in his eyes. He approaches.

COACH LUCAS
(friendly)
Morning, Charles.

CHARLES
(looking up, surprised)
Coach Lucas?

COACH LUCAS
Yes. Long time, isn't it?

They share a quiet moment, their past connection evident.

FADE OUT.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Charles and Coach Lucas sit across from each other, steaming lattes in front of them.

CHARLES
It's good to see you, Coach. How have you been?

COACH LUCAS
(waving it off)
I'm fine. But I didn't come here for a catch-up. I wanted to ask you something.

Charles raises an eyebrow.

FADE OUT.

INT. COACH LUCAS'S OFFICE - DAY

They sit in Coach Lucas's office, surrounded by trophies and sports memorabilia.

COACH LUCAS
You remember the Community Sports Program, right?

Charles nods.

COACH LUCAS
We're expanding it, making it bigger and better. And I want you to be a part of it.

CHARLES
(surprised)
Me? Why me?

COACH LUCAS
Because you have a gift, Charles. A unique perspective. And I believe it could make a difference in these kids' lives.

FADE OUT.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

Charles stands in front of a group of eager kids, all staring at him, expectantly. He takes a deep breath and begins to speak.

CHARLES
(encouraging)
Hey, everyone. I used to be a professional baseball player. But, as some of you might know, I had to retire early due to an injury. And for a while, I felt lost. But I realized something: I didn't need the game to be a part of me. I could be a part of the game. And that's what I want for all of you.

A wave of nods and smiles greets him.

FADE OUT.

INT. GYM - NIGHT

Charles is back on the elliptical, his mind racing with thoughts. Coach Lucas walks in, a knowing smile on his face.

COACH LUCAS
You're doing great, Charles.

CHARLES
(determined)
I'm just getting started.

FADE OUT.

EXT. BALL FIELD - DAY

Charles leads a group of kids through a baseball drill, his passion and energy palpable.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Charles and Coach Lucas sit, their lattes long gone, their eyes reflecting the sun-dappled scene outside.

CHARLES
(smiling)
This is more rewarding than any game I've ever played.

COACH LUCAS
(nodding)
I couldn't agree more.

They share a knowing look, their past struggles and triumphs united by their shared love for the game and their commitment to helping others.

FADE OUT.

INT. GYM - DAY

Charles, now a mentor and coach, works with kids, his eyes filled with hope and determination.

FADE IN:

TO BE CONTINUED...

END OF SCREENPLAY.
